description: Create and maintain API documentation from endpoint inventory through publishing.

steps.description: Catalog all API endpoints with their methods, parameters, and response shapes.

inputs.name: api-codebase
inputs.desc: Location of the API source code or route definitions

outputs.name: endpoint-catalog
outputs.desc: Every endpoint with method, path, parameters, request body, and response shape

outputs.name: undocumented-endpoints
outputs.desc: Endpoints found in code but missing from existing docs

process: Scan the codebase for route definitions and controller methods.
For each endpoint, record the HTTP method, path, path parameters, query parameters, request body schema, and response schema.
Compare against existing documentation and flag gaps.

steps.description: Generate request and response examples for each endpoint.

outputs.name: example-requests
outputs.desc: Sample request for each endpoint with realistic data

outputs.name: example-responses
outputs.desc: Sample success and error responses for each endpoint

process: For each endpoint, create a sample request with realistic parameter values.
Generate the expected success response matching the response schema.
Generate common error responses (400, 401, 404, 500) with error message format.

steps.description: Write the API documentation in a standard format.

outputs.name: api-reference
outputs.desc: Complete API reference documentation

outputs.name: getting-started-guide
outputs.desc: Quick start guide for new API consumers

process: Group endpoints by resource or domain area.
Write each endpoint section: description, authentication, parameters, request body, response, examples, error codes.
Write the getting started guide: authentication, first request, common patterns.
Add a changelog section for tracking updates.

steps.description: Publish the documentation and set up automated updates.

outputs.name: published-docs
outputs.desc: URL and access details for the published documentation

outputs.name: doc-update-process
outputs.desc: How documentation updates when the API changes

process: Choose the hosting platform for the documentation.
Publish the reference and getting started guide.
Set up a process to update docs when endpoints change (CI hook or review checklist).

description: Design and implement a webhook delivery system from registration through monitoring.

steps.description: Define the events that trigger webhooks and their payload schemas.

inputs.name: system-events
inputs.desc: List of events the system produces

inputs.name: consumer-needs
inputs.desc: What external systems need to know about

outputs.name: event-catalog
outputs.desc: Each webhook event with name, trigger condition, and payload schema

outputs.name: event-groupings
outputs.desc: Events grouped by resource for subscription management

process: List every event the system produces that external consumers would use.
Define the payload schema for each event: what fields, what format, what identifiers.
Group events by resource (e.g., order.created, order.updated, order.cancelled).

steps.description: Design the webhook subscription and registration API.

outputs.name: registration-api-spec
outputs.desc: API endpoints for creating, updating, listing, and deleting webhook subscriptions

outputs.name: security-spec
outputs.desc: Signature verification, secret rotation, and authentication for webhook delivery

process: Design CRUD endpoints for webhook subscriptions (create, read, update, delete, list).
Define the subscription fields: URL, events, secret, active/inactive status.
Design the signature scheme (HMAC-SHA256 with shared secret).
Add a test endpoint that sends a sample event to verify the consumer URL.

steps.description: Specify the delivery engine with retry logic and failure handling.

outputs.name: delivery-spec
outputs.desc: Delivery pipeline: queue, dispatch, retry, dead letter

outputs.name: retry-policy
outputs.desc: Retry schedule, backoff strategy, and failure thresholds

process: Design the delivery pipeline: event occurs, enqueue, dispatch to each subscriber, record result.
Define the retry policy: exponential backoff, maximum attempts, dead letter queue.
Specify failure handling: disable subscriptions after repeated failures, notify the subscriber.

steps.description: Design the monitoring and debugging tools for webhook delivery.

outputs.name: monitoring-spec
outputs.desc: Dashboard showing delivery success rates, latencies, and failures by subscriber

outputs.name: webhook-system-doc
outputs.desc: Complete webhook system documentation for both providers and consumers

process: Design a delivery log showing each attempt: timestamp, event, subscriber, HTTP status, latency.
Build a dashboard view: success rate by subscriber, by event type, over time.
Add alerting for subscribers whose failure rate exceeds the threshold.
Write consumer-facing documentation: how to register, verify signatures, handle retries.

description: Build an integration testing framework for API connections.

steps.description: Map all integration points between systems.

inputs.name: system-architecture
inputs.desc: How the systems connect to each other

outputs.name: integration-map
outputs.desc: Every integration point with source, target, protocol, and data flow

outputs.name: test-priority-ranking
outputs.desc: Integrations ranked by business criticality and failure risk

process: List every system-to-system connection.
For each connection, document the protocol (REST, GraphQL, message queue, file transfer).
Map the data flow: what data moves, in what format, how often.
Rank by priority: high-traffic and high-impact integrations first.

steps.description: Write test cases for each integration point.

outputs.name: test-cases
outputs.desc: Test cases covering success, failure, timeout, and data validation for each integration

outputs.name: test-data-requirements
outputs.desc: What test data is needed and how to generate or obtain it

process: For each integration, write test cases: successful data exchange, authentication failure, timeout, malformed data, rate limiting.
Define the expected behavior for each case.
Identify the test data needed: realistic payloads, edge cases, boundary values.
Document how to obtain or generate each test dataset.

steps.description: Set up the test runner and environment for integration tests.

outputs.name: test-environment-spec
outputs.desc: Environment configuration for running integration tests

outputs.name: test-runner-config
outputs.desc: Test runner setup with scheduling and reporting

process: Set up the test environment: staging endpoints, test credentials, network access.
Configure the test runner with scheduling (daily, on-deploy, on-demand).
Set up test reporting: pass/fail dashboard, failure alerts, trend tracking.

steps.description: Define the maintenance process for integration tests.

inputs.name: test-environment-spec
inputs.desc: How the test environment is configured

inputs.name: test-runner-config
inputs.desc: How tests are scheduled and reported

outputs.name: maintenance-process
outputs.desc: How to update tests when integrations change

outputs.name: integration-testing-doc
outputs.desc: Complete integration testing framework documentation

process: Define the process for updating tests when an API contract changes.
Set up contract change detection (schema diff, version bump alerts).
Document the full framework: how to add new integration tests, update existing ones, and interpret results.

description: Design an API versioning strategy from analysis through migration support.

steps.description: Analyze the types of changes the API undergoes and their impact on consumers.

inputs.name: api-history
inputs.desc: Past API changes and their effects on consumers

inputs.name: consumer-catalog
inputs.desc: Known API consumers and their usage patterns

outputs.name: change-taxonomy
outputs.desc: Types of changes (additive, breaking, deprecation) with historical frequency

outputs.name: consumer-sensitivity
outputs.desc: Which consumers are affected by which types of changes

process: Review past API changes and categorize them: additive (new fields/endpoints), breaking (removed/renamed fields), behavioral (logic changes).
For each consumer, determine which change types would break their integration.
Estimate the frequency of each change type going forward.

steps.description: Choose the versioning scheme and define the rules.

inputs.name: change-taxonomy
inputs.desc: Types and frequency of API changes

outputs.name: versioning-scheme
outputs.desc: Chosen approach (URL path, header, query param) with rules for when to increment

outputs.name: compatibility-rules
outputs.desc: What constitutes a breaking vs non-breaking change

process: Evaluate versioning approaches: URL path (/v1/), header (Accept-Version), query parameter.
Select the approach based on consumer needs and operational complexity.
Define the rules: what changes require a new version, what changes are backwards-compatible.

steps.description: Design the migration path for consumers moving between API versions.

outputs.name: migration-guide-template
outputs.desc: Template for consumer migration guides between versions

outputs.name: sunset-policy
outputs.desc: How long old versions are supported and how deprecation is communicated

process: Design the migration guide template: what changed, how to update, timeline.
Define the sunset policy: minimum support period, deprecation notices, shutdown timeline.
Define the communication plan: how consumers are notified of new versions and deprecations.

steps.description: Produce the complete API versioning strategy document.

outputs.name: versioning-strategy-doc
outputs.desc: Complete versioning strategy for the engineering team

outputs.name: consumer-versioning-guide
outputs.desc: Consumer-facing guide explaining how versioning works

process: Compile the internal strategy document: scheme, rules, processes, responsibilities.
Write the consumer-facing guide: how versions work, how to check your version, how to migrate.
Set a review cadence for the strategy.

description: Design a rate limiting system for an API.

steps.description: Profile current API traffic patterns to inform rate limit design.

inputs.name: api-logs
inputs.desc: Historical API request logs or metrics

inputs.name: consumer-tiers
inputs.desc: Different consumer types (free, paid, internal, partner)

outputs.name: traffic-profile
outputs.desc: Request rates by consumer, endpoint, and time of day

outputs.name: capacity-baseline
outputs.desc: Current system capacity and headroom

process: Analyze API logs for request rates by consumer, endpoint, and time period.
Identify peak traffic patterns and burst behavior.
Measure current system capacity and determine the headroom.

steps.description: Define rate limit policies for each consumer tier and endpoint.

outputs.name: rate-limit-policies
outputs.desc: Limits per consumer tier, per endpoint, with burst allowances

outputs.name: response-headers-spec
outputs.desc: Rate limit response headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, Remaining, Reset)

process: Set global rate limits based on system capacity.
Set per-tier limits: free (lowest), paid, partner, internal (highest or unlimited).
Set per-endpoint limits for expensive operations.
Define burst allowances and the throttling algorithm (token bucket, sliding window).
Define the response headers to include with every response.

steps.description: Specify the implementation: where limits are enforced and how violations are handled.

outputs.name: implementation-spec
outputs.desc: Where and how rate limiting is enforced (gateway, middleware, distributed counter)

outputs.name: rate-limiting-doc
outputs.desc: Complete rate limiting design document for engineering and consumers

process: Choose the enforcement point: API gateway, application middleware, or both.
Select the counter storage: in-memory, Redis, distributed cache.
Define the 429 response format: error message, Retry-After header, documentation link.
Document the system for both the engineering team and API consumers.

description: Design an API authentication and authorization flow.

steps.description: Gather authentication and authorization requirements from the API consumers and security team.

inputs.name: consumer-types
inputs.desc: Types of API consumers (server-to-server, user-facing app, third-party)

outputs.name: auth-requirements
outputs.desc: What needs to be authenticated, what needs to be authorized, what scopes exist

outputs.name: threat-model
outputs.desc: Authentication-related threats and mitigations

process: List each consumer type and how they will authenticate (API key, OAuth, JWT).
Define the authorization model: what resources, what actions, what scopes.
Identify authentication-related threats: token theft, replay, brute force.

steps.description: Select the authentication scheme and design the token lifecycle.

outputs.name: auth-scheme
outputs.desc: Chosen authentication scheme with token format, lifetime, and refresh strategy

outputs.name: scope-model
outputs.desc: Authorization scopes and how they map to API endpoints

process: Select the scheme: API keys for server-to-server, OAuth 2.0 for user-facing, JWT for stateless.
Define the token lifecycle: issuance, expiration, refresh, revocation.
Map scopes to endpoints: which scope grants access to which operations.

steps.description: Design the implementation details and error handling.

outputs.name: auth-endpoints-spec
outputs.desc: Token, authorize, and revoke endpoint specifications

outputs.name: error-responses-spec
outputs.desc: Authentication error responses (401, 403) with messages

process: Design the authentication endpoints: token exchange, refresh, revocation.
Define error responses: 401 (unauthenticated), 403 (insufficient scope), with actionable messages.
Specify rate limiting on authentication endpoints to prevent brute force.

steps.description: Produce the authentication flow documentation.

outputs.name: auth-flow-doc
outputs.desc: Complete authentication and authorization documentation

outputs.name: auth-quickstart
outputs.desc: Quick start guide for getting authenticated

process: Document the full authentication flow with sequence diagrams.
Write the scope reference: what each scope grants.
Write the quick start: how to get credentials, make the first authenticated request.
Document token management: storage, refresh, revocation.

description: Generate client SDKs from an API specification.

steps.description: Validate and normalize the API specification for SDK generation.

inputs.name: api-spec
inputs.desc: OpenAPI or similar API specification file

inputs.name: target-languages
inputs.desc: Which programming languages to generate SDKs for

outputs.name: validated-spec
outputs.desc: API specification that passes validation and is ready for code generation

outputs.name: spec-issues
outputs.desc: Any issues found and resolved in the specification

process: Run the specification through a validator (OpenAPI linter or equivalent).
Fix any errors or inconsistencies.
Normalize naming conventions for SDK-friendly code generation.

steps.description: Generate the SDK code and customize it for each language.

outputs.name: generated-sdks
outputs.desc: Generated SDK code for each target language

outputs.name: customization-notes
outputs.desc: Language-specific customizations applied

process: Run the code generator for each target language.
Apply language-specific conventions: naming, error handling, async patterns.
Add authentication helpers: configure once, use everywhere.
Add pagination helpers for list endpoints.

steps.description: Test each SDK against the API and prepare for publishing.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: SDK test results against the live or staging API

outputs.name: sdk-packages
outputs.desc: Packaged SDKs ready for distribution

process: Write integration tests for each SDK: authentication, CRUD operations, error handling.
Run tests against the staging API.
Package each SDK for its language's package manager.
Write the README for each SDK: installation, authentication, basic usage.

steps.description: Set up the SDK update process for when the API changes.

outputs.name: sdk-update-process
outputs.desc: How SDKs are regenerated when the API changes

outputs.name: sdk-generation-doc
outputs.desc: Complete SDK generation and maintenance documentation

process: Set up a CI pipeline that regenerates SDKs when the API spec changes.
Define the versioning strategy for SDKs relative to the API version.
Document the full process: generation, customization, testing, publishing, maintenance.

description: Set up API monitoring from metric definition through alerting.

steps.description: Define the metrics that indicate API health.

inputs.name: api-architecture
inputs.desc: How the API is deployed and what it depends on

outputs.name: health-metrics
outputs.desc: Metrics to track: latency (p50, p95, p99), error rate, availability, throughput

outputs.name: metric-thresholds
outputs.desc: Normal, warning, and critical thresholds for each metric

process: Define the core metrics: request latency percentiles, error rate, availability, requests per second.
Add dependency metrics: database latency, cache hit rate, external API latency.
Set thresholds based on SLA requirements: what is normal, what triggers a warning, what triggers an alert.

steps.description: Build the API monitoring dashboard.

outputs.name: monitoring-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard showing real-time API health across all metrics

outputs.name: dashboard-layout
outputs.desc: How the dashboard is organized for incident response

process: Design the dashboard layout: overview panel (status, key numbers), detailed panels by metric category.
Add time-range selectors for investigating incidents.
Add endpoint-level drill-down for isolating problems.
Include a dependency health panel.

steps.description: Configure alerting rules and escalation paths.

outputs.name: alert-rules
outputs.desc: Alerting rules with conditions, severity, and notification channels

outputs.name: api-monitoring-doc
outputs.desc: Complete API monitoring and alerting documentation

process: Write alert rules for each threshold: warning (notify channel), critical (page on-call).
Add compound alerts: error rate AND latency spike indicates a different problem than either alone.
Document the runbook: when this alert fires, check these things in this order.
Compile the monitoring documentation.

description: Manage the lifecycle of deprecating and removing API endpoints.

steps.description: Identify endpoints that should be deprecated and assess the impact.

inputs.name: api-usage-data
inputs.desc: Which endpoints are called, by whom, and how often

inputs.name: deprecation-reasons
inputs.desc: Why each endpoint is being considered for deprecation

outputs.name: deprecation-candidates
outputs.desc: Endpoints to deprecate with usage data and impact assessment

outputs.name: affected-consumers
outputs.desc: Which consumers use each endpoint and how to reach them

process: Pull usage data for the candidate endpoints: request volume, unique consumers, last 90 days trend.
For each endpoint, identify every consumer that has called it recently.
Assess the impact: how many consumers, how critical is their usage, is there an alternative.

steps.description: Write the deprecation plan with timeline and migration path.

inputs.name: deprecation-candidates
inputs.desc: Endpoints to deprecate with impact data

inputs.name: affected-consumers
inputs.desc: Who is affected and how to reach them

outputs.name: deprecation-timeline
outputs.desc: Schedule: announcement, sunset warning, removal date

outputs.name: migration-guide
outputs.desc: How consumers should migrate to the replacement endpoint or approach

process: Set the timeline: announce deprecation (day 0), add deprecation headers (day 0), sunset warning period, removal date.
Write the migration guide: what to use instead, how to update calls, code examples.
Plan the communication: changelog entry, email to affected consumers, documentation update.

steps.description: Execute the deprecation plan and monitor migration progress.

outputs.name: migration-tracking
outputs.desc: Dashboard showing consumer migration progress

outputs.name: deprecation-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the deprecation for future reference

process: Add the Deprecation and Sunset response headers to the affected endpoints.
Send the initial communication to affected consumers.
Track migration progress: are consumers switching to the replacement?
At the removal date, verify all active consumers have migrated, then remove the endpoint.

description: List an integration in a marketplace from packaging through launch.

steps.description: Package the integration for marketplace submission.

outputs.name: package-bundle
outputs.desc: Integration packaged according to marketplace requirements

outputs.name: marketplace-requirements-checklist
outputs.desc: Marketplace submission requirements with completion status

process: Review the target marketplace's submission requirements.
Package the integration: code, configuration, dependencies.
Verify the package meets all technical requirements: size limits, API versions, permissions.

steps.description: Write the marketplace listing content.

outputs.name: listing-content
outputs.desc: Title, description, screenshots, category, and tags for the listing

outputs.name: setup-documentation
outputs.desc: End-user setup guide for the integration

process: Write the listing title and description focused on what the integration does for the user.
Create screenshots or diagrams showing the integration in action.
Choose the correct category and tags.
Write the setup documentation: prerequisites, installation steps, configuration, first use.

steps.description: Review and submit the listing, then handle the review process.

outputs.name: submission-status
outputs.desc: Status of the marketplace review and any feedback to address

outputs.name: marketplace-listing-doc
outputs.desc: Complete record of the listing: what was submitted, where it is listed, how to update it

process: Review the complete submission against the marketplace checklist.
Submit the listing and track the review status.
Address any review feedback and resubmit if needed.
Once approved, document the listing URL, update process, and support responsibilities.
